**Binary search time complexity: O(log n)** on a sorted array.

Each comparison discards half of the remaining elements, so the number of steps grows as log2(n).

Key points:

- Space: O(1) for the iterative version; O(log n) for the recursive version because of the call stack.
- Prerequisite: the data must already be sorted. If it is not, sorting first dominates the total cost at O(n log n).
- Worst-case comparisons for n elements: at most floor(log2(n)) + 1.
- Best case: O(1) when the target is the midpoint on the first check.
